editorial.headline: Wholesale Musical Instruments: Nationally Open, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This wholesale activity spans traditional and modern musical instruments, open nationally to full foreign ownership but blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Wholesale trade in musical instruments covers a broad and distinctly cultural as well as commercial field. Its scope includes traditional instruments such as kecapi, bamboo flutes, calung, angklung, kolintang, gamelan, rebab, rebana, tifa and sasando, alongside modern instruments including flute, saxophone, harmonica, trombone, guitar, mandolin, ukulele, harp, bass, violin, cello, piano, organ, drums and tuning forks. The defining feature is wholesale trade: the activity concerns these instruments as a category, whether rooted in Indonesian musical traditions or in contemporary instrumental practice.

The activity is open to businesses at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In practical terms, the national record permits full foreign ownership for this activity; it does not set a foreign stake below full ownership. The applicable national source recorded for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali presents a different result. A foreign investor cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today. The Bali status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO: at Besar scale, every scope is assessed in OSS as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah risk, placing the activity within Bali’s province-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. The recorded reason identifies the moratorium as taking effect in May 2026. This is not a national foreign-ownership restriction; nationally the activity remains open to 100% foreign ownership. It is a Bali-specific bar on PMA registration, driven by the local risk-classification rule.

That distinction matters most where a business plan is geographically specific. The national position describes the permitted ownership structure for the activity. Bali’s position determines whether a PMA registration for it can proceed on the island at all. For wholesale musical-instrument trade, the national door is open; the Bali PMA route is not.
